state:
**Goal `path-literals-follow-up`: Stage 2 is on disk, and Stage 3 is next.** Stage 1's floor is goal `plain-comments`'s list.

Every attack under `tests/hostile/` that ends early declares `// hostile: ends-early <step> <ending>` and prints `step <N>` as the first statement of that step (`rule:testing/hostile-case-contract`, ADR 0244). `tools/nv/proofs/run.ts:@judgeHostile` fails a case whose marker is malformed or names a step that is not the last, one that stopped before the step, and one that stopped with another ending; `tools/nv/test/hostile-ending.test.ts` pins the verdicts and reads every attack. The step line is matched at the end of a line, because a response body written before it may not end its own line. The ending of a throw is the first report's `class`: a hook that throws while the failure is reported writes a second report after it.

The migration found one real failure: `Core\Http\Client::openSocket` checked a header with a line break only after it connected, outside a test. It is now checked before the connect in both paths (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/http/socket.rs:420`), and that attack reaches its last step and stops with `FATAL`.

Eight attacks are slow or still fail on their own known gap, and declare `FATAL` because that is what they are written to reach: the five marked `proof: gap`, plus `core/Heap/peek/01`, `core/Request/query/01` and `core/Xml-Reader/read/01`, which time out under the debug `nvs` and stop with `FATAL` under the proof binary.
